3D printer bed sizes, and the largest piece you can print

The build volume of popular 3D printers, with the largest single piece PrintSlice makes for each one at default settings. If your model is bigger than your bed, PrintSlice splits it into pieces this size or smaller and adds connectors so they fit back together.

PrinterBuild volume (mm)Largest piece (mm)
Bambu Lab A1 mini 180 × 180 × 180 168 × 168 × 168 Split for this bed
Bambu Lab A1 256 × 256 × 256 244 × 244 × 244 Split for this bed
Bambu Lab P1S / P1P / X1 Carbon 256 × 256 × 256 244 × 244 × 244 Split for this bed
Bambu Lab H2D (single nozzle) 325 × 320 × 325 313 × 308 × 313 Split for this bed
Creality Ender 3 / Pro / V2 / V3 SE 220 × 220 × 250 208 × 208 × 238 Split for this bed
Creality Ender 3 S1 220 × 220 × 270 208 × 208 × 258 Split for this bed
Creality K1 / K1C 220 × 220 × 250 208 × 208 × 238 Split for this bed
Creality K1 Max 300 × 300 × 300 288 × 288 × 288 Split for this bed
Elegoo Neptune 4 Pro 225 × 225 × 265 213 × 213 × 253 Split for this bed
Original Prusa MK4 / MK4S 250 × 210 × 220 238 × 198 × 208 Split for this bed
Original Prusa MINI+ 180 × 180 × 180 168 × 168 × 168 Split for this bed
Prusa CORE One 250 × 220 × 270 238 × 208 × 258 Split for this bed

Build volumes are X × Y × Z, from each maker's published specifications (checked October 2026). "Split for this bed" opens PrintSlice with that size filled in.

Questions

What does build volume mean?

It's the largest box your printer can print in one go: X is left to right, Y is front to back and Z is height. Makers also call it the print size or bed size.

Why is the largest piece smaller than the bed?

PrintSlice keeps 5.6 mm clear on every side by default: a 2 mm safety margin you can change, plus 3.6 mm so a connector tab sticking out of a piece still fits on the bed. That's 11.2 mm off each axis in total.

How many pieces will my model need?

Divide each side of your model by your printer's largest piece size, round each answer up, and multiply the three together. For example, a 400 × 200 × 100 mm model on a 220 × 220 × 250 mm bed needs 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 pieces.

What if my printer isn't listed?

Look up its build volume on the maker's spec page, open PrintSlice and type the three numbers into the bed-size fields.

Does PrintSlice cost anything?

Splitting and previewing is free, with no account needed. To download the pieces you create a free account and start a 7-day free trial (a card is needed, but you aren't charged until the 7 days are up and you can cancel before then). After that it's £3.99 a month.
